title: The Intervention Trigger Ledger
subtitle: Turn one early customer signal into a bounded, reviewable action before the aggregate score changes.
intro_text: Use this ledger for one recurring customer risk. Define the consequence, source, baseline, trigger rule, verification step, response, and reset condition before the next signal appears.
scoring_note: Do not create a trigger score. Record a decision rule, test it against known timelines, and review the resulting action.
closing_quote: A signal earns intervention rights only when the team knows what changed, compared with what, for how long, and what happens next.
next_action: Choose one recurring risk. Complete one ledger entry, test it against three historical or illustrative timelines, then run it prospectively without changing the aggregate health score.
interpretation: The signal is visible but the trigger rule is not met
The rule is met but evidence quality or customer context needs confirmation
The rule is met, verified, and linked to a named customer consequence
Action, owner, due date, and communication
The signal repeatedly creates noise or does not change a useful decision
Reason, replacement, or activity to stop

sections.title: Customer Consequence and Signal
sections.why_it_matters: An early metric matters only when it is connected to a customer decision, milestone, or outcome.
sections.review_prompt: What customer consequence could this signal reveal early enough to change?
rows: Which decision, milestone, or outcome may be affected?
What exact observation may change before the consequence?
Which system or human record supplies it?
How current and complete must the evidence be?

sections.title: Baseline and Trigger Rule
sections.why_it_matters: Without an explicit baseline and window, normal variation becomes arbitrary escalation.
sections.review_prompt: Compared with what, for how long, does the observation become decision-relevant?
rows: Expected pattern for this customer, workflow, and stage
Direction and magnitude of the meaningful deviation
Seasonality, rollout phase, planned change, or missing data

sections.title: Verification and Response
sections.why_it_matters: A trigger should create a bounded action, not an unexplained red flag.
sections.review_prompt: What must be confirmed, who acts, and by when?
rows: Data-quality and customer-context evidence to confirm
Observe, verify, or intervene based on consequence and timing
The exact play, decision, or customer action created
Who needs an update and what decision is requested?

sections.title: Reset and Learning
sections.why_it_matters: A trigger without a reset and review rule becomes permanent risk theatre.
sections.review_prompt: What closes this trigger, and how will the team learn whether it deserved action?
rows: Observable condition that closes or downgrades the trigger
Date the trigger must be revalidated or retired
Normal variation or data defect that created avoidable work
Did the action change the customer decision or milestone?
